claim: truncate_utf8_by_bytes tests whether the input fits by comparing Str.length (a code-point count) with the byte budget, so an input with at most n code points but more than n bytes is returned whole: "é" (C3 A9) with max_bytes=1 returns 2 bytes.
notes: Line 22 `let n = Str.length(s)`; the else-branch slices bytes. Spotted on reading, then confirmed by execution on two routes: the private function called directly (direct.sh, store.ail verbatim plus an appended driver) and the exported store_stdout_and_elide (via_store.ail, conformance canned_ports). Sweeps: 30,716 of 223,159 (seed 1) and 124,448 of 434,052 (seed 2) cases with n>=0 violate it, identical on both routes. Every violation satisfies Str.length(in) <= n < |in| with out == in, using the runtime's own counts; result is up to 4x n (emoji). Reachable: compose.ail:723 is the only caller, with max_stdout_bytes = clamp_positive(cfg, 4000) (compose.ail:851). Production-shaped witness `P6.1 4000 e4b8ad*2000` (2,000 x U+4E2D, 6,000 bytes) comes back whole at 6,000 bytes with truncated=true and "[stdout elided; full output at ...]" appended, and that is ComposeResult.stdout (compose.ail:753). Negative control T6_MUTANT=fix_len (`let n = length(b);`, applied to the generated copy only): P6.1 holds on all cases and this repro exits 0.

claim: Known K2: when the input does not fit, the function cuts at byte n with no regard to character boundaries, so a valid UTF-8 input gives invalid UTF-8: "éa" (C3 A9 61) with max_bytes=1 returns the single byte C3.
notes: Registered as known-violated (K2); re-confirmed on the real code, not new. Sweeps: 10,911 of 104,747 (seed 1) and 47,193 of 319,979 (seed 2) valid-UTF-8 cases, the same set via store_stdout_and_elide. std/bytes.toString does not repair (the bytes come back raw), so P6.2 holds: in all 168,698 and 246,898 cut cases the result is exactly the first n bytes. Fixing A2-T6-1 makes this more frequent (30,465 under T6_MUTANT=fix_len), because more inputs then reach the cut. Reachable through compose.ail:723 to ComposeResult.stdout; RESEARCH §7 notes that the JSON encoder later writes U+FFFD per invalid byte.

claim: The TypeScript twin truncateUtf8ByBytes (src/tui/src/compose-claimcheck.ts:104) decodes the cut bytes with Buffer.toString("utf8"), which replaces a split character with U+FFFD, so its text is not a byte prefix of the input and can exceed maxBytes: "é" with maxBytes=1 gives EF BF BD (3 bytes), reported as 0 bytes omitted.
notes: X-1 = P6.1 and P6.2 stated on the twin's `text`, reached through the exported runClaimCheck with a stub callStream that captures the informalizer prompt. Seed 1 (valid UTF-8, n>=1; 78,280 runs): byte bound violated in 26,042, prefix violated in 29,913, P6.3 holds in all. Seed 2 (270,077 runs): 104,984, 121,798 and 0. The twin differs from the AILANG function on 41,346; under the fix_len mutant the difference is exactly the 30,465 cases where the AILANG result is invalid UTF-8. The prefix fails without the bound failing on `X-1 3 f09f9880` (😀 cut to 3 bytes becomes EF BF BD). Overshoot is at most 2 bytes. omittedBytes = max(0, |in| - |text|) understates whenever text grows, and is 0 for the witness although the whole input was dropped. Reachable: env-server.ts:1810 runs claimcheck on raw compose stdout with AILANG_COMPOSE_CLAIMCHECK_STDOUT_MAX_BYTES (default 4000); the text goes into the informalizer prompt. env-server.ts:377 has the same body but no callers (read only, not executed).

claim: store_stdout_and_elide (store.ail:32-49, the target's only caller) discards the ok/error of p.dir_make and p.file_write: with ports that refuse both, it still returns "...[stdout elided; full output at <raw_path>]" and nothing in its result reports that the full output was never written.
witness: stdout "abcd" (61626364), max_stdout_bytes=3, conformance canned_ports() (dir_make and file_write answer ok=false)
notes: Outside the target's lines 19-29; reported as another defect in the code path that reaches the target. The result record {stdout, truncated, raw_path, next_state} has no place for the failure. The ABI's ExtFileMutation carries ok/error so that callers do not drop a failed write (motoko-ext-abi/types.ail, WI-D17 comment); every file_write in store.ail drops it (lines 36, 65, 80-81), so this is a module-wide pattern. Severity is low: when the write fails, the agent is pointed at a file that may not exist, and the clipped output is all it gets. Not a registered property.
